title: Publish Audit Event Schema v1 + schema evolution rules and examples for SIEM export
creator: Kevin Osei
description:
Goal
Publish and operationalize Audit Event Schema v1 for SIEM-ready audit export (beta). This includes:
- A stable, versioned event envelope suitable for Splunk/Datadog/S3 sinks
- Clear schema evolution/backward compatibility rules
- Concrete examples for high-signal events (login, key rotation, RBAC changes, export config change)
- PII/redaction guidance so we do not leak secrets while still being SIEM-correlatable

Background / Why
We need a schema that:
1) supports correlation across systems (request_id, actor, workspace/tenant, resource, environment, IP/geo)
2) is stable enough for customer parsers + dashboards
3) can evolve without breaking existing pipelines (Splunk sourcetypes, Datadog pipelines, S3 lake ingestion)

This ticket is the engineering deliverable that turns PM-4822 taxonomy decisions into a published and enforced v1 contract.

Deliverables
1) Audit Event Schema v1 document
- Canonical field list with types and required/optional markers
- Field naming conventions (snake_case), timestamps (RFC3339), IDs (UUID), and enums
- Event type taxonomy (top-level categories and event_type strings)
- PII classification and redaction rules

2) Schema evolution plan
- How we represent versioning (event.schema_version)
- Backward compatibility guarantees
- Deprecation policy and timelines
- Guidance to customers for parsing (e.g., treat unknown fields as ignorable; do not assume ordering)

3) Examples
- JSON examples for the common event types we expect to validate in beta
- Examples should include all correlation-relevant fields and illustrate optional/null cases

Proposed schema (v1) - high level
Event envelope (all events):
- schema_version (string, required): "1.0" for v1 beta. MUST be present on every event.
- event_id (string UUID, required): unique per emitted audit event. Used for dedupe.
- occurred_at (string RFC3339, required): when the audited action occurred.
- received_at (string RFC3339, required): when event entered the audit pipeline (control plane).
- event_type (string, required): stable identifier, e.g. "auth.login.succeeded".
- severity (string, optional): "info" | "warning" | "critical" (initially info/warning only).
- tenant_id (string, required): Redwood tenant/workspace identifier.
- environment (string, required): "hosted" | "dedicated" | "private".
- region (string, optional): Redwood region (e.g., "us-east-1"); for Private may be "customer".

Actor (who performed the action):
- actor_type (string, required): "user" | "service_account" | "api_key" | "system".
- actor_id (string, required except system): Redwood internal ID for principal.
- actor_display (string, optional): email/handle if permitted (see PII guidance).
- actor_ip (string, optional): client IP (may be omitted for Private if not available).
- actor_user_agent (string, optional): user agent string (truncate to max length).
- actor_region (string, optional): coarse geo derived from IP (country/region). DO NOT include precise location.

Action / Target (what happened):
- action (string, required): normalized verb, e.g. "create" | "update" | "delete" | "rotate" | "login".
- resource_type (string, optional): e.g. "api_key" | "rbac_role" | "audit_export_destination".
- resource_id (string, optional): stable identifier for the resource.
- resource_name (string, optional): display name (non-sensitive).
- outcome (string, required): "success" | "failure".
- failure_reason (string, optional): stable code only (no secrets). e.g. "invalid_credentials".

Correlation (cross-system joins):
- request_id (string, optional): Redwood request id for control plane/API requests.
- trace_id (string, optional): tracing id if available.
- session_id (string, optional): for Console auth flows.

Metadata
- redwood (object, optional): internal-only metadata SHOULD NOT be exported. If present internally, exporter drops it.
- additional_context (object, optional): strictly allowlisted key/value pairs; must pass validation and redaction.

Important: The above should be represented as a flat JSON object where possible. Where nested objects are used (actor/target), keep depth <= 2 and avoid polymorphism.

PII / Redaction rules (v1)
- NEVER include:
  - raw credentials (API keys, OAuth tokens, Splunk HEC tokens, Datadog API keys)
  - request/response bodies
  - prompt content, model outputs, customer data payloads
- Actor display fields:
  - actor_display may include user email for Hosted/Dedicated if tenant has not disabled it (future toggle). For beta: include email for Console users; for service accounts prefer name.
  - actor_user_agent allowed but truncated (e.g., 256 chars) to avoid exfil.
- IP address:
  - actor_ip is allowed for security correlation; treat as sensitive and document that customers are responsible for downstream handling.
- additional_context is allowlisted per event_type; values must be scalar (string/number/bool) and capped.

Schema evolution rules (contract)
- Version field: schema_version is a string "MAJOR.MINOR".
  - v1 starts at "1.0".
- Backward compatible changes (minor bump, e.g., 1.0 -> 1.1):
  - adding new optional fields
  - adding new event_type values
  - widening enums by adding values (never removing)
  - adding new optional additional_context keys
- Breaking changes (major bump, e.g., 1.x -> 2.0):
  - removing or renaming fields
  - changing field types
  - changing semantic meaning of existing fields
  - changing required/optional in a way that breaks parsers
- Deprecation policy:
  - Deprecate fields/event_types with notice in release notes.
  - Keep deprecated fields for >= 2 minor versions or >= 90 days (whichever longer) before major bump.
- Parser guidance for customers (must be in docs):
  - treat unknown fields as ignorable
  - do not rely on field ordering
  - dedupe using event_id (and destination + time window) due to at-least-once delivery

Implementation notes
- Schema MUST be enforced at export boundary (before enqueue) to prevent poison-pill events reaching sinks.
- Exporter should include schema_version in every record.
- For S3 sink (JSON lines): one event per line, UTF-8, newline-delimited, no trailing commas.
- For Splunk HEC: event payload uses HEC "event" field; ensure schema_version/event_type are in root of event.
- For Datadog logs: include service/source tags (e.g., source=redwood-audit) without mutating schema fields.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Confluence page updated/created for Audit Event Schema v1 with the above rules and examples
- [ ] Schema file stored in the canonical location referenced by exporter + control plane (internal repo or schema registry path)
- [ ] Exporter validation updated to require schema_version and required v1 fields
- [ ] Documented evolution policy included in SIEM export docs (customer-facing summary + internal details)
- [ ] Security + GRC sign-off (Marcus + Olga) that PII/redaction guidance is sufficient for beta

Open questions
- Should we represent actor/target as nested objects (actor.{id,type,...}) vs flattened fields for easier SIEM parsing? Current proposal is flattened to reduce nested parsing issues. Confirm with Solutions (Colin/Fatima) for Splunk CIM alignment.
- Do we need a dedicated "workspace_id" separate from tenant_id for multi-workspace orgs, or is tenant_id the workspace? PM-4822 to confirm.
- For Private deployments, do we always have actor_ip? If not, ensure it is optional and absence is documented.
